headline_marked: Iran warns [[conflict with US won't end in surrender]] as hostilities resume
headline: Iran warns conflict with US won't end in surrender as hostilities resume
summary: Top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says Tehran is prepared to defend itself after tit-for-tat attacks between the two nations.
details: Iran's top negotiator and parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, stated that the ongoing confrontation with the United States will never end with Iran's surrender.

The remarks follow a week of tit-for-tat attacks, where Washington accused Tehran of targeting commercial ships, leading to US strikes, which Iran responded to by attacking US assets in Middle Eastern countries with drones and missiles.
This escalation comes just over three weeks after both nations signed an agreement intended to turn a months-long ceasefire into a durable peace.
Ghalibaf revealed that during negotiations with US Vice President JD Vance, he explicitly stated that Iran has no trust in the US government.
The Iranian official emphasized that those capable of negotiating with America are those who are prepared for war, asserting that Tehran will stand firm to secure the Iranian people's rights.
Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump has agreed to further negotiations, despite repeating his assertion that the previous ceasefire between the two countries is over.
A delegation from Qatar, acting as a mediator, has arrived in Iran to facilitate talks following the latest escalation.
caption:

headline: Belgium failed to beat Spain in last 11 meetings, facing them in World Cup quarterfinal
summary: Spain enters the clash with a record six straight World Cup clean sheets, while Belgium boasts one of the tournament's highest shot-conversion rates.
details: Spain and Belgium face off in a World Cup quarterfinal clash on Friday. Spain arrives as the tournament's smoothest operator, while Belgium is emboldened by a recent 4-1 victory over the United States.
Belgium has struggled against Spain, failing to beat them in their last 11 meetings across all competitions. In their last five encounters, they have lost by an aggregate score of 13-1.

Spain's defense has been nearly impenetrable, reaching the quarterfinals without conceding a goal in five matches. This is a first since Italy in 1990, and they have gone over 10 hours of play without conceding a goal.

Belgium's attacking efficiency is high, with a second-highest recorded shot-conversion rate of 12.1% at a World Cup since 1966. They are averaging 21.4 shots per game, totaling 107 shots in five matches.
Lamine Yamal has been a standout performer for Spain, completing 17 dribbles—the most by any player in this edition of the tournament.
Rodri has recorded 80 line-breaking passes, the most by any Spanish player at a World Cup since 2010.
Belgium's Romelu Lukaku is likely to start on the bench again, despite scoring in three straight World Cup matches. All three of his goals this tournament have come as a substitute.
Under manager Luis de la Fuente, Spain has progressed from all six of their major-tournament knockout games.
With 13 goals scored, Belgium ranks second for goals scored in the tournament, so far, behind France and Argentina.
caption:
Belgium hasn't won against Spain in 11 games. Can they break the curse in the World Cup quarterfinals?

Spain and Belgium face off in a World Cup quarterfinal clash on Friday. Spain arrives as the tournament's smoothest operator, while Belgium is emboldened by a recent 4-1 victory over the United States.

Belgium has struggled against Spain, failing to beat them in their last 11 meetings across all competitions. In their last five encounters, they have lost by an aggregate score of 13-1.

Spain's defense has been nearly impenetrable, reaching the quarterfinals without conceding a goal in five matches. This is a first since Italy in 1990, and they have gone over 10 hours of play without conceding a goal.

Belgium's attacking efficiency is high, with a second-highest recorded shot-conversion rate of 12.1% at a World Cup since 1966. They are averaging 21.4 shots per game, totaling 107 shots in five matches.

Lamine Yamal has been a standout performer for Spain, completing 17 dribbles—the most by any player in this edition of the tournament.

Rodri has recorded 80 line-breaking passes, the most by any Spanish player at a World Cup since 2010.

Belgium's Romelu Lukaku is likely to start on the bench again, despite scoring in three straight World Cup matches. All three of his goals this tournament have come as a substitute.

Under manager Luis de la Fuente, Spain has progressed from all six of their major-tournament knockout games.

With 13 goals scored, Belgium ranks second for goals scored in the tournament, so far, behind France and Argentina.
